# Admin API authentication

## Internal mode

The default. Requests are served without authentication when they come from a trusted network (loopback by default, your cluster or host network if you add it); every other request is refused. Right when your backend runs next to the agent.

## Corporation mode

Set `ADMIN_API_AUTH_MODE=corporation`, `ADMIN_API_PUBLIC_URL` (the public origin of the admin API), and `ADMIN_API_CORPORATION_ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS` (the accounts allowed to call). Trusted networks keep working without authentication; external callers authenticate with their account key:

```bash
# 1. a nonce for the caller's account
curl -s -X POST https://admin.agent.example.com/v2/auth/challenge -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"account":"verana1…"}'            # -> nonce, expiresAt, audience
# 2. sign "vs-agent-admin-auth:<audience>:<nonce>" with the account key (ADR-036), then
curl -s -X POST https://admin.agent.example.com/v2/auth/token -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"account":"verana1…","pubKey":"<base64>","signature":"<base64>","nonce":"<nonce>"}'   # -> token, expiresAt
# 3. call with Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

The challenge never reveals whether the account is allowed; the refusal happens at the token or the call. Tokens live in memory and die with a restart. The agent publishes a `VsAgentAdminAPI` entry in its DID Document so callers discover the origin from the DID.

This is the mode the Verana MCP server and external operator consoles need. Keep the allowlist to the operator accounts that need it.

## Health endpoints

Liveness and readiness are served without authentication in both modes and never answer `401` or `403`.
